stance_summary: The manuscript is stuck because it treats the five-layer architecture as the payload; every candidate below moves the payload elsewhere (a physics result, a measured retrieval benchmark, a released resource, a git-verifiable failure dataset) or falsifies the genre guess that is blocking the user.
anchored_assumption: The user is silently assuming that (a) the AI agent must be the SUBJECT of the paper rather than the instrument, and (b) 'we have no data' is a fact about the world rather than a fact about where they looked; in reality the deployed system has already generated two years of pre-existing, non-fabricable, timestamped evidence (git history, 571 wiki provenance pointers, a 199-citation ledger, a 62k-paper corpus with a labeled read-set) that was recorded BEFORE this paper existed and therefore is not self-serving, and 'they do not accept practice reports' is an unverified guess marked with 应该 that has never been checked against the journal's own back issues.

candidates.one_line: Flip subject and instrument: write a genuine nuclear-physics research article whose result is a cross-literature methodological claim that the wiki actually surfaced (e.g. the EC vs POD-Galerkin equivalence in synthesis/ec-vs-pod-galerkin-same-method.md), verified numerically with the user's own existing emulator codes, with the agent architecture demoted to a short methods section plus a provenance ledger.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Open /Users/jinlei/research-wiki/synthesis/ec-vs-pod-galerkin-same-method.md together with the claim lines of its linked eigenvector-continuation and reduced-basis source pages, and write one page stating the equivalence as a falsifiable proposition plus the exact numerical test that would break it (which two emulators, which system such as d+58Ni or n+90Zr, which observable, and the number of significant figures that counts as agreement).
candidates.cost_estimate: 3 to 5 weeks total: 1 day to fix the proposition and test, 3 to 5 days of numerics on SLAM.jl / the RB emulator on heliumx, 1 week for figures via nature-figure, 1.5 to 2 weeks of Chinese writing to 5000-8000 characters. The physics half of the citations is already read literature, so the reference list is cheap.
candidates.info_gain: If it works, the special issue gets a paper with real numbers that no referee can call self-evaluation, and the AI angle becomes credible precisely because it is subordinate: the agent found the equivalence across 42 read papers, the physics verifies it. If it fails, the user learns whether the wiki's synthesis pages contain any claim that is genuinely novel and checkable, which is itself a decisive verdict on whether the knowledge system produces research output or only organization, and that verdict is worth more than the manuscript.
candidates.risk: The equivalence may already be published explicitly in the EC literature, in which case the physics payload evaporates and the numerics were wasted, worst case about 1 week. Mitigation is a literature-corpus plus literature-search novelty scan on day 1 before any compute. Secondary risk: the paper becomes so physics-centric that it no longer reads as an AI-agent paper for the special issue, which is a framing problem in the introduction, not a data problem.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: The artifact kind changes from a framework description to a physics result with numerical verification; the existing 4596 characters survive only as a compressed methods section.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: This is the opposite genre claim: not an experience report at all but an ordinary 原创研究论文 whose evidence is coupled-channel numerics, the genre the journal explicitly accepts.

candidates.one_line: Stop describing the three-layer literature stack and measure it: turn the 62k-paper corpus plus the 571 already-labeled wiki provenance pointers into a standard retrieval benchmark (recall@k, MRR, missed-citation exposure rate) whose ground-truth labels were written years before this paper existed.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Sample 50 claims in the wiki that already carry an explicit source pointer, run literature-corpus BM25 over the 62k nucl-th corpus with the claim text as the query, and record the rank at which the true supporting paper appears; report recall@1, recall@5, recall@20 and the number of complete misses.
candidates.cost_estimate: 2 to 4 weeks: 1 day for the 50-claim pilot, about 1 week to scale to a few hundred claims and add the 199-citation review ledger as a second evaluation set, 1 week of analysis and figures, 1 week of writing. All local, no new tooling.
candidates.info_gain: Either way the user obtains the first quantitative characterization of his own discovery layer. If recall is high, the paper gets a defensible Results section with real numbers and the normative claim that lexical misses are not novelty proof becomes a measured statement rather than an assertion the wiki context flags as unanchored. If recall is low, that is the more interesting result and directly changes the user's own submission workflow, which is worth more than the paper.
candidates.risk: The residual overlap with T3 is the strongest failure mode: a referee may still read it as the author grading his own system. The defense must be structural, that the labels are pre-existing and the metric is a standard IR metric over an external 62k corpus, not an author-authored question set with author-assigned scores. If that defense is judged insufficient, about 1 week is lost. Second risk: corpus licensing may block release of the evaluation set, which weakens reproducibility.

candidates.one_line: Reclassify the contribution from framework to released resource, following the resource/database-paper genre used in astronomy and bioinformatics and already used by the user himself for COLOSS and HPRMAT: publish a sanitized, citable subset of the nuclear-reaction concept wiki plus the unified vocabulary and schema, and let the paper describe and quantitatively characterize the released object.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Write the export inclusion/exclusion rule (which page types and which frontmatter fields ship, with reviews/, drafts, unpublished results, collaborator notes and anything gitignored excluded by rule not by inspection), then run one dry-run pass that counts how many pages and vocabulary terms survive the rule.
candidates.cost_estimate: 3 to 5 weeks: 1 day for the rule and dry run, 1 week to build and audit the sanitized export including a manual leak check, 1 week to compute coverage statistics against an independent reference list, 1 to 2 weeks of writing. The confidentiality audit is the unavoidable slow part.
candidates.info_gain: If it works, the paper stands on an artifact readers can download and check, which is the same evidential basis as the user's own accepted code-release papers, and the framework prose becomes documentation rather than the claim. If it fails, either because too little survives sanitization or because the surviving subset is not useful to anyone else, the user learns that the knowledge base's value is irreducibly personal, which settles the genre question permanently and stops further attempts to package it as a community contribution.
candidates.risk: Confidentiality is the sharp edge: the wiki contains referee material, unpublished manuscripts and collaborator correspondence, and the paper additionally requires a 保密审查 certificate. A single leak in the export would be far worse than a rejection. Worst case is 2 weeks spent on an export that the sanitization rule reduces to something too thin to publish. Secondary risk: 《核技术》 may not treat a knowledge-base release the way CPC treats a code release.

candidates.one_line: Promote §5 from caveat to primary result: mine two years of git history across both wikis for every commit that corrects, reverts or downgrades a previously AI-written claim, and publish the measured failure taxonomy of a deployed research-agent knowledge system, with incident records that are timestamped and not fabricable.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Run git log with diff search over ~/research-wiki and ~/research-wiki-personal for commits whose message or diff reverses an earlier claim (corrections, reverts, 'downgraded', 'corrected from', deleted assertions), dump the matching commits to a table with date, page, and the before/after claim text, and count how many fall into each of the five failure modes already named in §5.
candidates.cost_estimate: 2 to 3 weeks: 1 day for the git mining pass, 3 to 4 days to classify and check each incident against what actually happened, 1 week to write it as a taxonomy with per-mode mitigation and evidence of whether the mitigation held afterwards, plus figure work. Cheapest of the five paths.
candidates.info_gain: If the incident count is substantial and cleanly classified, the paper acquires the one thing a self-reported system paper normally cannot have, namely evidence that hurts the author, which is exactly the evidence a PRC referee trusts; and each mitigation can be checked for recurrence after its fix date, giving a real before/after signal on the same timeline. If the count is small or the incidents will not classify, the user learns his §5 taxonomy is inherited from general AI discourse rather than from his own deployment, which should change §5 regardless of which paper he writes.
candidates.risk: Some of the most instructive incidents touch confidential material (referee handling, unpublished manuscripts, an editorial screening record kept in an embargoed directory), so the publishable subset may be much smaller than the mined set. Worst case is 1 week to discover that only a handful of incidents can be described publicly. Secondary risk: an honest failure catalog may read as an argument against the framework, so the recurrence-after-mitigation analysis must be present or the paper undercuts itself.

candidates.cost_estimate: 1 to 2 days for the survey itself. The full path is short by design: the survey ends with a genre decision that then feeds whichever of A1 to A4 the evidence supports, so its own cost is bounded and it is the only path that can be abandoned at zero loss.
candidates.info_gain: If the journal has published methodology or software papers as 研究论文, the entire blocking assumption dissolves and the existing 4596 characters need only length and evidence work rather than a genre change. If it has not, the user gets the first hard evidence for a belief he currently holds on intuition, which converts a hesitation into a decision and justifies the cost of A1 to A4. Either branch resolves in under two days.
candidates.risk: The journal's archive may be paywalled or awkward to enumerate, capping the sample at abstracts and titles, which makes genre classification noisy; worst case is half a day lost. A subtler risk is over-reading the result: a genre that appeared once is not proof of acceptance, so the survey should report counts rather than a verdict, and it must not become a substitute for actually strengthening the evidence in the manuscript.
